items.title: Pentagon, Lockheed agree to decade-long F-35 framework deal for hundreds of jets
items.snippet: The tentative agreement, which still needs lawmakers’ blessing, covers production and sustainment over the 10 years.
items.summary: The Pentagon and Lockheed agreed to a tentative F-35 framework covering production and sustainment over the next 10 years; lawmakers must still approve it.
items.why: The framework concerns long-term fighter production and sustainment.

items.title: USAF Confirms Bombers Could Have A Major Air-To-Air Combat Role
items.snippet: Bombers are now being viewed as another potential air-to-air asset on top of growing the fighter fleet and establishing a CCA force. The post USAF Confirms Bombers Could Have A Major Air-To-Air Combat Role appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone reports that the USAF sees bombers as a potential air-to-air asset, alongside expanding the fighter fleet and establishing a CCA force.
items.why: A possible air-to-air role could affect how bombers contribute to combat operations.

items.title: Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production
items.snippet: The KJ-3000 is the most capable of China’s rapidly expanding airborne early warning and control aircraft fleet. The post Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone says four KJ-3000 radar jets at a Chinese factory point to serial production. It describes the aircraft as China’s most capable airborne early warning and control aircraft.
items.why: The aircraft fleet’s expansion is relevant to airborne surveillance and control capabilities.

items.title: Are yearlong deployments the Navy’s new normal?

items.summary: That's what officials are telling sailors' families in Japan, where two destroyers are slated for 12- and 14-month cruises.

items.title: Ground-Launched Rusty Dagger Low-Cost Cruise Missile Seen For The First Time
items.snippet: The first public look at the missile in a surface-launched configuration comes as its manufacturer expands production. The post Ground-Launched Rusty Dagger Low-Cost Cruise Missile Seen For The First Time appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone reports the first public look at the Rusty Dagger low-cost cruise missile in a surface-launched configuration, as its manufacturer expands production.
items.why: A surface-launched configuration and expanding production are relevant to missile deployment and availability.

items.title: Space Force shifts into high gear on cislunar warfare, with RFIs coming soon
items.snippet: Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, the Space Force’s portfolio acquisition executive for advanced programs, said the service wants to field cislunar capabilities by the end of fiscal 2029.
items.summary: Breaking Defense reports that the Space Force wants to field cislunar capabilities by the end of fiscal 2029, according to Gen. Stephen Purdy.
items.why: Cislunar capabilities extend military planning into the space between Earth and the Moon.

items.title: Brothers in Arms, Partners in Healing: A Story about a Breakthrough in Treating Post-Traumatic Stress
items.snippet: After losing fellow marines in Iraq, Jeff Lindquist struggled with post-traumatic stress that was steadily destroying his life. Years later, an innovative technology helped him reclaim it. This is the story of Jeff and Erik Won, two veterans who served together, and how efforts to help Jeff recover was the first step o
items.summary: War on the Rocks tells the story of veterans Jeff Lindquist and Erik Won, and an innovative technology that helped Lindquist reclaim his life after post-traumatic stress.
items.why: The story highlights technology's role in treating post-traumatic stress among veterans.

items.title: A-4 ‘Super’ Skyhawks Playing The Bad Guys In European Skies
items.snippet: The A-4 Skyhawk, first flown seven decades ago, is famed for its role as a Cold War 'red air' aggressor, and it lives on doing that mission to this day in Europe. The post A-4 ‘Super’ Skyhawks Playing The Bad Guys In European Skies appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The A-4 Skyhawk continues to fly red-air aggressor missions in Europe, according to The War Zone.
items.why: The aircraft’s continued use highlights the role of aggressor platforms in training against simulated adversaries.

items.title: Trump says Musk has restored access to Ukraine's Starlink network
items.snippet: Ukraine relies on Starlink for a range of military uses - its owner Elon Musk has repeatedly denied restricting access.
items.summary: The BBC reports that Trump says Musk restored Ukraine’s access after a Starlink dispute. It says Ukraine relies on Starlink for military uses, while Musk has denied restricting access.
items.why: Ukraine’s reliance on Starlink makes access to the service strategically relevant to its military.

items.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
items.snippet: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk says the multiple attacks may amount to war crimes.
items.summary: A BBC investigation finds Sudan's RSF fighters deliberately targeted hospitals. The UN human rights chief says the multiple attacks may amount to war crimes.
items.why: The allegations highlight the strategic and humanitarian significance of attacks on hospitals in Sudan.
